_comment: Cookie Run OvenBreak (com.devsisters.crg) run-grind with Multi-Buy Double Coins. All coords verified live @1920x1080. INVARIANT: never Play without Double Coins equipped — the only exception is an empty wallet (nocoins -> insufficient_coins -> force_play). Every path to Play must first observe either the doublecoins_banner or the 'Not enough Coins!' popup. Loop: home->Play->boost_shop->probe_dc_owned(skip buy if banner already up)->buy_boost->Multi->picker->Multi-Buy->wait_roll->start_run: banner up = Play, banner absent = retry_buy -> buy again. RELAY MISS FIX (2026-08-09): live-caught on boxrun_speed — the 'Save the Cookie' Pit-Lift-purchase screen (mid-run near-death prompt, 'X for 1 Pit Lift' bar) can appear the SAME instant as the Cookie Relay prompt; the relay text was genuinely on screen (watcher score 0.72, above the 0.62 threshold) but the bot's own poll landed on the frame just before it rendered and read absent, then walked straight to the next hop without rechecking — the relay was gone by the time the chain came back around. All relay_stage1/2_* and relay_poll1/2_* states now carry absent_retries=2/absent_wait_ms=400 (~2.8s grace incl. poll overhead, same mechanism probe_dc_owned already used) so a same-frame miss gets rechecked in place instead of being abandoned for a whole hop cycle.

home._note: Main menu, detected by the 'Play!' button (home/home_play_marker.png). The OLD marker cropped the 'Episode 1' banner text, which SILENTLY BROKE the whole bot once the account advanced past Episode 1 — the banner text changes per episode, so home stopped matching (score ~0.43 vs the 0.82 threshold), every loop fell through to `running`, and `running`'s blind relay tap at (960,540) landed on a leaderboard friend row, opening the Friend's Info popup stack the bot then got stuck behind. 'Play!' is episode-independent (score 1.000 across episodes; popups/modals score 0.24-0.32). Play! visible = nothing covers it, so tap it directly. Absent -> either a modal covers it or we're elsewhere: hand off to probe_sendlife, the head of the modal-peeling chain (NEVER blind-tap from here). The 4500ms wait after the tap covers the boost-shop load: at 3000ms the shop screen was often still fading in with Play! underneath (score ~0.87, over the 0.82 threshold), so guard_not_home read it as 'still on home' and bounced back here for a wasted second tap.

await_shop._note: Bridge between tapping Play! on home and acting in the boost shop. The shop fades in over a variable time, and while it fades the Play! button shows THROUGH it above the 0.82 threshold — so if home went straight to boost_shop, an early miss sent us to running -> guard_not_home (sees Play!) -> home -> tap Play AGAIN. Measured on a full day of logs that second-tap loop fired ~11.7 times PER run (home-Play taps 2521 vs boost-shop Play 216), wasting ~25s/run and risking a stray tap landing on a shop cell. Here we wait for the shop to actually settle: on_match = shop is up, proceed to the coin guard. Absent = still fading (or we were never in the shop): peel a retry via await_shop_2 instead of bouncing back to home. The wait+re-check replaces blind reliance on one fixed 4500ms sleep.

await_shop_2._note: Second (final) shop-settle re-check. Shop up -> coin guard. Still absent after this second wait -> we are genuinely not in the shop (bot started mid-run, or a run auto-started), so fall through to running and let the guard chain sort out where we actually are. Only ONE bounce back into the running/guard machinery, not an unbounded loop.

probe_dailycheckin._note: New head of the modal-peeling chain. The 'Daily Check-in' calendar pops ONCE per day at first launch and sits ON TOP of home, hiding Play! — with no dismiss the bot stalls (falls through to boost_shop and never recovers home). Detected by the unique 'Daily Check-in' banner title (dailycheckin_marker: self=1.000, in-run=0.232 — no false-positive). Present -> tap the green OK button (965,985) -> probe_treasurereward (a second launch popup often queues behind it). Absent -> fall to probe_treasurereward too. Shared with boxrun_default.json; same template, same coords.

probe_treasurereward._note: The 'Power+ Treasure Rewards' popup stacks right after Daily Check-in at launch and also covers Play!. Detected by the unique 'Power+ Treasure Rewards' title (marker self=1.000, in-run=0.31, vs dailycheckin=0.40 — no cross-match). Present -> tap Confirm (960,850) -> home. Absent -> fall to probe_sendlife. Shared with boxrun_default.json.

probe_sendlife._note: Reached whenever Play! is not visible and no launch popup was on screen. A 'Send <friend> a free Life? (+N Gift Points)' dialog pops over home when a stray in-run tap lands on a leaderboard friend row. Tap Cancel (727,688 — gray, left) to dismiss; NEVER Confirm (1189,687 — green) since we don't want to burn gift interactions. Detected by the unique 'Gift Points' text. Dismissed -> back to home to re-check Play!. Absent -> not this modal; try the boost shop next (we may simply be in it).

boost_shop._note: boost shop open. BEFORE buying anything, route through probe_dc_owned: if the Double Coins banner is already up (boost equipped from a previous multi-buy — e.g. bot restarted after a roll landed but before the run consumed it), buying again just burns coins. Only when the banner is absent do we proceed to buy_boost.

probe_dc_owned._note: COIN GUARD: Multi-Buy must fire ONLY when Double Coins is NOT already equipped. boxrun/doublecoins_banner.png (same template start_run uses) shows on the boost-shop right panel whenever the boost is active. Present -> skip the whole buy flow, go straight to the Play gate. Absent -> buy_boost opens the Multi picker as before. RETRY GRACE (3x800ms): the equipped-boost banner takes ~1-2s to render after the shop opens, so detecting with no grace read the still-fading panel, thought the boost was absent, and re-bought/re-rolled every cycle — burning coins. Same fix as boxrun_magnet probe_magnet.

buy_boost._note: No Double Coins equipped (probe_dc_owned confirmed banner absent). Tap the Random Boost gift box cell to make the right panel show Random Boost + Multi, then open the Multi picker.

picker._note: Pick desired Boosts popup. Double Coins stays pre-ticked by default — DO NOT tap it (the row is a toggle; tapping un-ticks it). Tap Multi-Buy ONCE — the game then AUTO-ROLLS by itself, repeatedly, until the ticked boost (Double Coins) lands, then stops on its own. A 'Stop'/progress animation plays the whole time. We must NOT tap Stop or anything else during it, and must NOT re-open Multi/re-buy — the game is already rolling. Hand off to wait_roll to sit still until the roll UI is gone. ABSENT means the picker never opened (the Multi tap missed, or the popup was still animating in past the 1500ms wait) — the old config sent that straight to wait_roll, whose marker is also absent (nothing is rolling), so the bot fell all the way through check_boost_result -> start_run -> Play with NO boost at all. Observed live 2026-07-12 01:13:13-01:13:20: buy cell + Multi tapped, no Multi-Buy tap ever logged, Play tapped 5s later. Now: settle-and-recheck via picker_2 (same pattern as await_shop/await_shop_2) instead of assuming a roll happened. TICK GUARD (2026-08-02): the rows are toggles and the game REMEMBERS ticks across sessions, so 'the boost we want is pre-ticked' is only true until something else changes it — another bot config, a --boost run through run_toggle.py, or a manual tap. Found live with '+17% base speed' ticked and Magnetic Aura/Double Coins NOT, which would make Multi-Buy roll for the wrong boost, start_run's banner check fail, and retry_buy re-roll until the coins ran out. The prelude below now clears every other row and ticks ours before Multi-Buy, mirroring what src/boost.py's apply_boost injects for the toggle family. Each tap is `optional` + roi-scoped: 'template absent' means the row is already in the wanted state, so it is a no-op, not an error.

picker_2._note: Second (final) picker-settle re-check. Popup finally up -> tap Multi-Buy and roll as normal. Still absent -> the picker genuinely never opened, so NO roll is in flight: do NOT fall through to Play (that was the bug). Go to retry_buy, which re-checks coins and re-opens the buy flow.

wait_roll._note: The self-rolling Multi-Buy is in progress: the game keeps re-rolling and spending coins until the chosen boost lands, showing a Stop button (rollstop_marker) the WHOLE time. Self-loop while Stop is present so we never cut the roll short. FIX: the old multibuy_marker was the GREEN Multi-Buy button that starts the roll — it vanishes the instant the roll begins, so wait_roll exited immediately, start_run read a still-rolling (boost-absent) banner, and the loop re-bought forever, draining coins. rollstop_marker (the Stop button, shown throughout the roll) is the correct signal. Stop gone -> roll finished -> read the banner in start_run. Shared with boxrun_magnet. absent is a goto to a DIFFERENT state (start_run) so self-loop + timeout is safe. match_timeout_ms 90000 bounds a roll UI stuck matched forever — the state's timeout_ms only ever fired on the absent path.

insufficient_coins._note: SAFETY: 'Not enough Coins!' popup (auto-buy ran the balance dry). Tap Cancel (770,685) — NEVER Confirm (1150,685), which spends gems. Then Play! with whatever boost we have (or none).

force_play._note: Coins exhausted — stop chasing Double Coins, Play! with whatever boost we have. Still route through check_heart so we don't try to run on empty hearts.

start_run._note: HARD RULE: never Play without Double Coins. This state is the enforcement point. Reached only AFTER wait_roll confirmed multibuy_marker is gone, so no roll is in flight and it is safe to act. Banner present -> the roll landed Double Coins -> check_heart -> Play. Banner ABSENT -> the roll ended on some OTHER boost (or the picker never opened at all) -> we do NOT own Double Coins -> retry_buy, which buys again until we do. Previously BOTH branches went to check_heart, making the detect meaningless: any non-DC outcome silently Played with the wrong boost — the bug this file was changed to fix. The only sanctioned way to Play without Double Coins is the nocoins escape (insufficient_coins -> force_play).

retry_buy._note: Re-buy gate: we ended up without Double Coins (wrong boost rolled, or the picker never opened) and must buy again. Check the wallet FIRST so we never spin re-opening the shop on an empty balance: 'Not enough Coins!' up -> insufficient_coins (Cancel, then force_play with whatever we have — the ONLY sanctioned Play-without-DC path). No popup -> coins remain, so loop back into buy_boost. Termination is natural rather than a retry counter: the FSM has no state variables, so counting rounds would need a chain of retry_1..retry_N states; instead each buy drains coins until the game itself raises nocoins, which ends the loop. A genuinely stuck loop still trips the engine's livelock warning (100 identical polls -> Discord alert).

check_heart._note: SINGLE Play gate, reached from await_shop/boost_shop (Play at 1365,931). boxrun/heart_empty.png = separator '|' + FIRST (leftmost) heart gray, cropped live at 0 hearts — hearts deplete right-to-left, so slot 1 is gray ONLY at 0 hearts. CV: 0 hearts=1.000; 1-3 hearts ~0.75 (thin margin, don't raise match_threshold). Present -> close the boost shop popup IF one is open (this state is reached via await_shop -> probe_speed with the shop possibly still open — its own tap-Play path tolerates that because Play shows through the fade, but the errands below need a clean home screen or their own detects miss everything behind the shop; live-verified 2026-08-08, the very first run through this path hung for 500+ polls on sendlife_mailbox's open_mailbox because the shop was still covering the mailbox icon). tap_template with optional=true, not close_popup: this state is also reached with --boost none (boost_skip_goto skips the shop chain entirely), where no shop popup exists at all and close_popup's unconditional blind tap at the shop's X coordinate would land on whatever home element happens to sit there instead — optional means absent is a normal outcome, not a retry target. Then run the Send-Life and mailbox-sweep errands (their own configs, each ending in their own `stop`) instead of idling here: 0 hearts means 25+ min of dead air before regen, so the wait is put to use on friend-list upkeep rather than burned sitting on a 30s self-loop. Send-Life only clears the Episode already selected on home (no episode switching — that would leave the wrong Episode selected when boxrun resumes); the mailbox sweep runs its own full loop. Then re-check check_heart: still 0 -> another errand pass; a heart regenerated meanwhile -> falls straight through to the on_absent Play path below. Absent (>=1 heart) -> tap Play then SPAM-TAP the Fast Start spot (985,515) across the prompt window into the run (blind spam, ported from boxrun_magnet — more robust than detect+tap which missed when the prompt window was short).

running._note: In-run (auto-play). Result popup up -> run over. Not up -> we might still be running, but we might equally be sitting on home or in the shop, so DON'T tap yet: hand off to the guard chain, which only lets the jump/relay taps fire once it has ruled out every static screen those taps could damage. (Previously this state's on_absent fired jump + tap(960,540) unconditionally; with the home marker broken that tap kept landing on the home leaderboard and opening friend popups.)

guard_not_home._note: Guard 1/2 before any in-run tap: is the Play! button on screen? If so we're on home, not running — go handle home instead of tapping the leaderboard.

guard_not_shop._note: Guard 2/2: are we in the boost shop? If so resume the buy loop rather than tapping. Only when neither Play! nor the shop is visible do we accept 'we are mid-run' and fire the jump + Cookie Relay Boost taps — a random point in the left jump zone (~238,940), ~35% of the time a quick double-jump, plus the relay icon at mid-screen (~960,540). The two zones don't overlap, so both are safe to fire together once we know we're actually in a run. The guards ran on the SAME capture as `running`, so reaching here costs nothing extra; the jump is the first thing that invalidates the frame. Hand off to the fast-jump chain (jump_2..jump_4) instead of straight back to the probe chain: measured on 10,204 real jumps, routing every single jump through check_shop_after_run + the 6 probe states cost a second full capture (~850ms) and stretched the median jump gap to 3s — longer than the ~1.5-2s a pit stays on screen, so the bot was missing pits structurally. The probes only ever fired on 0.8% of cycles (84 popups all day), so they do not need to run every cycle. Neither Play! nor shop visible -> guard_not_sendlife (rule out a Send-Life/Level-Up popup before assuming genuinely mid-run and jumping blind).

guard_not_sendlife._note: Guard 3: a "Send <name> a free Life?" dialog can pop mid-loop when a stray tap grazes a leaderboard friend row (we are actually still on the Friends-tab home, not mid-run). Detect it and Cancel (727,688 — gray/left, NEVER Confirm) -> home. Absent -> guard_not_levelup. Ported from boxrun_passive.

guard_not_levelup._note: Guard 4: a "Level Up" reward popup (levelup_marker, self=1.000) can pop mid-loop from auto-play XP gain — same class as Send-Life. Confirm (959,969, same coord as probe_levelup) -> home. Absent -> genuinely mid-run -> resume the original jump/relay action (moved here from guard_not_shop) and hand to jump_2. Ported from boxrun_passive.

jump_2._note: Fast-jump hop 2/4. One capture per hop, and that capture is spent on the single question that matters mid-run: has the result popup appeared? If not, jump again immediately. NO relay tap here — the relay icon sits at screen centre (960,540) and, when the run has actually ended without us noticing, that tap lands on the home leaderboard and opens the Friend's Info popup stack. Firing it once per four jumps instead of once per jump cuts that exposure ~4x while still triggering the boost (10,297 relay taps all day for one boost each run is wild overkill). RELAY REVERTED: (490,955) was misread from a partner-count BADGE, not the actual relay button. The Cookie Relay Boost tap is screen-centre (960,540) as originally verified — restored here. RELAY (2026-08-03): the blind relay_tap here is gone. After the hop action we go through relay_stage1_jump_3/relay_stage2_jump_3, which detect the real two-stage Cookie Relay prompt and resume at jump_3 either way.

jump_3._note: Fast-jump hop 3/4. Same contract as jump_2. RELAY REVERTED: (490,955) was misread from a partner-count BADGE, not the actual relay button. The Cookie Relay Boost tap is screen-centre (960,540) as originally verified — restored here. RELAY (2026-08-03): the blind relay_tap here is gone. After the hop action we go through relay_stage1_jump_4/relay_stage2_jump_4, which detect the real two-stage Cookie Relay prompt and resume at jump_4 either way.

jump_4._note: Fast-jump hop 4/4 — last hop before we pay for a housekeeping pass. Falls through to check_shop_after_run, which re-checks home and then walks the whole probe chain (levelup / ranking / giftdraw / friendinfo / congrats). Popups do not expire on their own, so sweeping them once every 4 jumps (~4-5s) clears them just as reliably as sweeping every jump did, at a quarter of the capture cost. RELAY REVERTED: (490,955) was misread from a partner-count BADGE, not the actual relay button. The Cookie Relay Boost tap is screen-centre (960,540) as originally verified — restored here. RELAY (2026-08-03): the blind relay_tap here is gone. After the hop action we go through relay_stage1_check_shop_after_run/relay_stage2_check_shop_after_run, which detect the real two-stage Cookie Relay prompt and resume at check_shop_after_run either way.

check_shop_after_run._note: Result popup not up yet — either still running, home is back, or we entered mid-boost_shop. Try home; on timeout fall through to boost_shop so a wrong entry point self-recovers instead of spinning forever.

probe_boostshop._note: Recovery probe: are we actually sitting in the boost shop (e.g. process started there, or run ended straight into shop)? If so, resume the buy loop; else check for a level-up popup.

probe_congrats._note: Level-up 'Congratulations!' popup (free reward, e.g. Treasure Ticket) appears over home after enough XP. Confirm (956,846) collects it — this Confirm is safe/free, unlike the nocoins Confirm. Then back to waiting.

probe_levelup._note: A separate 'Level Up' popup (gems/coins/score-bonus reward, distinct screen from the Congratulations ticket popup) can also appear after a run. Confirm (959,969) is safe/free — collects the reward.

probe_rankingrewards._note: SAFETY NET: a stray in-run relay tap (~960,540) can hit the leaderboard and open the gold 'Ranking Rewards' season-reward popup over home, which the probe chain otherwise can't clear (home_marker fails behind it) -> loop spins to max_cycles. Detected by the gold 'Ranking Rewards' title ribbon. Tap its single X (1672,135 — CV verified) to close; free/safe, no currency. Then back to home.

probe_giftdraw._note: SAFETY NET: 'Gift Draw' popup (100 Gift Points -> free gift box) can appear over home, e.g. after collecting enough points from daily login/send-life/invite. Detected by the teal 'Gift Draw' banner. Tap the X close (1685,170 — CV verified on the banner crop) rather than Draw, since we don't want to auto-spend/auto-consume the gift draw as part of the farm loop. Then back to home.

probe_friendinfo._note:
SAFETY NET: 'Friend's ___' popup family, which can stack two layers. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-06 (frames archived as docs/evidence/friendinfo_stacked_2layers.png and docs/evidence/friendinfo_single_layer.png):
• ONE layer ('Friend's Info' alone) — (1633,107) IS the X and closes it in a single tap, 0.974 -> 0.343.
• TWO layers ('Friend's Cookie' over 'Friend's Info') — the inner card covers (1633,107) (that pixel reads BGR 85,85,85, a shadow) and the inner X sits at about (1555,125). Tapping the outer coordinate hits nothing, so no retry count clears both layers from one coordinate.
LIVELOCK CONFIRMED (2026-08-08, live logs 02:57-03:09 and 12:51-13:04, 34 consecutive WARNINGs each episode, ~12min each): the stacked case scored 0.98 across all 3 close_popup retries because every attempt tapped the SAME outer coordinate ±10px — none ever reached the inner card's X. After exhausting retries the state gave up and jumped to `running`, which polished on relay/jump states for a mid-run screen that was never actually there, then looped back to probe_friendinfo ~15s later and repeated — an unbounded loop the log never showed as "stuck" because each pass did produce activity (taps, transitions), just none of it against the real screen.
FIX (2026-08-09): the previous note said "do NOT add a second blind tap" — correct for an UNSCOPED tap, which the 2026-08-06 attempt was and which fired on home whenever the popup was already gone (see docs/evidence for why). The fix here is different: a ROI-scoped tap_template against friends/friendcookie_innerclose.png (a generic circular-X crop) restricted to a ROI around the inner X.
ROI WIDENED 2026-08-14 after a third variant turned up. Scanning all 1,401 archived unknown_screens frames for friendinfo_marker found 12 hits, hashes all distinct (11 separate events 08-03..08-11 plus one on 08-14), and they split into THREE layouts, not two:
• 'Friend's Info' alone — X at (1638,107), bbox (1598,68,80,78), pixel (1633,107) is the white glyph. close_popup handles it.
• 'Friend's Cookie' over Info — inner X bbox (1500,101,76,79), template centre (1570,127). The original roi=[1520,90,120,80] covered exactly this one (1.000) and nothing else.
• 'Friend's TREASURE' over Info — the common case, 11 of the 12 frames, identical coordinates every time: inner X bbox (1368,50,80,76), template centre (1423,88). The old ROI scored only 0.453 here, BELOW the 0.82 threshold, so the fallback never fired on the variant that actually keeps happening.
roi=[1360,50,240,110] covers both stacked layouts and still ignores what it must. VERIFIED THROUGH src.perceive.find, not a hand-rolled slice: 0.997 on all 11 Treasure frames (tap lands 1423,88), 1.000 on the Cookie frame (1570,127), 0.252 on the single-layer frame, and 0 false positives across 178 random non-friendinfo frames. A first attempt at [1350,50,240,80] looked correct against a hand-written slice that padded the box by the template size; the real ROI crops the frame to exactly (x,y,w,h) and requires the whole 55x55 template to fit inside it, so that box scored 0.169 on the Cookie layout — below threshold, silently reintroducing the bug it was meant to fix. Measure candidate ROIs by calling find() with roi=..., never by slicing the frame yourself. optional:true means a pass where only one layer exists is a silent no-op, not an error. Sequence: close_popup(outer, retries=1) → tap_template(inner, ROI-scoped, optional) → wait → close_popup(outer, retries=1) again to clear whatever layer is left — covers single-layer (first close_popup succeeds, inner tap is a no-op, second close_popup finds nothing and verifies clean) and two-layer (first close_popup fails on the outer coordinate every time, inner tap actually closes the Friend's Cookie card, second close_popup then reaches and closes the now-exposed Friend's Info X) without a blind unscoped tap ever firing.

run_result._note: Result popup after a run. Tap OK (702,940) — NOT 'Show Off' (blue, opens social share). After OK a Mystery Box popup sometimes appears -> mystery_box handles it.

mystery_box._note: After Result-OK we either land on home, or a 'Mystery Box' screen blocks it (only on runs whose Result showed a box icon). Detect the BOX screen positively rather than inferring it from 'home is absent': the old version blind-tapped the screen centre (960,540) whenever home didn't match, and since the old home marker was episode-specific it stopped matching entirely — so every Result landed a tap on the home leaderboard, opening a friend popup. Box present -> tap it open (960,540 is the closed box) and go read the reward. Box absent -> we're on home (or a modal over it); let the home state / probe chain sort it out.

mystery_box_recheck._note: After collecting the box: Play! visible -> home is clear, continue. Not visible -> something still covers it; go through probe_sendlife (the modal-peeling chain) rather than `running`, whose on_absent blind-taps the screen centre and would hit the leaderboard.

probe_connectionlost._note: Connection Lost — server drop popup, can appear anywhere (head of the probe chain since nothing else works while offline). Text: 'Connection lost! Tap Confirm to restart the game and reload your data.' Not a dismiss: Confirm (960,700) actually restarts the client, so we hand off to restart_app (cycles the process the same way session_reset does) then the existing recover_login chain re-auths. Absent -> probe_inactive (rest of the popup chain).

probe_enterleague._note: Enter League — 'You have been entered in a League. Check out your position in the League Ranking!' Random season-start popup, can appear anywhere. Plain dismiss: Confirm (960,700) just closes it, no restart needed. Absent -> probe_inactive (rest of the popup chain).

probe_inactive._note: Home-side inactive guard. 'You've been inactive for a while. The game will restart!' can queue on/over home after a long idle. Confirm (953,690) lets the restart proceed, then hand to recover_login to re-auth. Absent -> probe_prevresults.

probe_prevresults._note: 'Previous Results / You have unreviewed game results' pops after a run that was cut short (e.g. by the inactive-restart). Confirm (950,680) opens the Result screen, then fall through to the normal chain which peels Result/MysteryBox/Congrats. Absent -> probe_dailycheckin (chain unchanged).

guard_not_inactive._note: Mid-run inactive guard. The inactive-restart popup can fire WHILE a run is on screen (Jump/Slide visible) when the bot stops feeding input -> observed live hanging the run. Confirm (953,690) -> recover_login re-auths. Absent -> the run is genuinely live: fall through to the original mid-run action (unchanged). RELAY REVERTED: (490,955) was misread from a partner-count BADGE, not the actual relay button. The Cookie Relay Boost tap is screen-centre (960,540) as originally verified — restored here. RELAY (2026-08-03): the blind relay_tap here is gone. After the hop action we go through relay_stage1_jump_2/relay_stage2_jump_2, which detect the real two-stage Cookie Relay prompt and resume at jump_2 either way.

recover_login._note: Login recovery step 1 (DevPlay title). After the inactive-restart the game reopens on the DevPlay title with the orange 'DevPlay Login' button (devplaylogin_marker, self=1.0). Present -> tap it (960,950) to open the account picker, wait for the fade, hand to recover_pick. Absent -> we may already be at the picker (or past login) -> recover_pick.

verify_no_popup._note: Play-tap gate. The 'You've been inactive -> restart' popup overlays home/shop while Play! still scores ~0.87 through it, so home.on_match would tap Play INTO the popup and spin. Check inactive_marker first: present -> Confirm (953,690) -> recover_login re-auths. Absent -> no popup, run the real Play tap (original home.on_match body).

recover_pick._note: Login recovery step 2 (account picker). login_marker = 'You already have an account!' + CookieRun logo (name-agnostic). Present -> tap the top saved account row (1100,490), wait out the ~12s login + home load, re-enter start_state (home). Absent -> the picker isn't up (login already completed, or the title is still animating) -> go to start_state and let its own detection settle; if we're still on the title, home will be absent and the probe chain loops us back to recover_login.

verify_no_sendlife._note: Second Play-tap gate. A 'Send <name> a free Life?' dialog can sit ON TOP of home (or the boost shop) while Play! still scores 1.00 through it, same class of bug as the inactive-popup gate. Present -> Cancel (727,688 — gray/left, NEVER Confirm 1189,687) -> back to home to re-check. Absent -> no popup at all -> run the real Play tap (original verify_no_popup.on_absent body, unchanged).

verify_no_prevresults._note: Third Play-tap gate. 'Previous Results / You have unreviewed game results' sits ON TOP of home while Play! still scores 1.00 through it — same class of bug as the inactive and send-life gates. Without this the loop taps Play into the dialog forever: the popup does not cover the button, so home matches, the two existing gates find nothing, and probe_prevresults (which does handle it) is only reachable when home is ABSENT. Present -> Confirm (950,680), verified, then back to home. Absent -> the real Play tap.

verify_no_enterleague._note: Fourth Play-tap gate. The Enter League dialog is centred and leaves the Play button uncovered, so home matches at 1.00 through it and the loop would tap Play into the dialog — the same trap Previous Results fell into. probe_enterleague handles the popup but only runs when home is ABSENT. Present -> Confirm (960,700), verified, back to home. Absent -> the real Play tap.

probe_settings._note: User can manually open Game Settings (gear icon, top-right of home) at any time, on any tab (Options/Notifications/Performance/Game Info) -- no marker recognized this screen before, so the bot sat frozen matching nothing. Detect the teal 'Game Settings' title ribbon (shared by all 4 tabs); close via X (1671,145) -> home re-checks. Absent -> continue the normal chain.

probe_fortunebakery._note: 'Fortune Bakery' popup (fortune-cookie dough picker) can sit over home, covering Play!, with no auto-buy risk on our side (we never tap Select Dough). Detected by the teal 'Fortune Bakery' banner (boxrun/fortunebakery_marker.png). Close via X (1633,301 — scaled from a 1217x703 screenshot ratio, NOT yet CV-verified live; re-crop/re-measure on first live catch if the tap misses). Absent -> probe_prevresults (chain unchanged).

mb_open._note: Mystery Box screen — one self-looping dismiss state (replaces the mb_gate/mystery_box_reveal/mb_reveal_gate/mb_reveal_retry_2..6 chain, which claimed to cap at 6 dual-taps but retry_2 looped straight back to mystery_box_reveal so _3.._6 were dead and the loop was unbounded; mb_gate/mb_reveal_gate also detected inactive_marker while their notes described the Mystery Box screen). Each pass taps Open-all (960,965), box-center (960,540) and per-item Confirm (959,960) — covers both known layouts, a tap that hits nothing is harmless. Marker gone -> mystery_box_recheck. match_timeout_ms is the REAL bound on a stuck MATCH (timeout_ms only fires on the absent path). An inactive popup here covers the marker -> absent path -> recheck -> home's probe chain reaches recover_login, so the per-pass inactive check the old gates did is redundant.

probe_news._note: 'News' popup (patch notes / new-treasure announcements) opens ON TOP of home and fully covers Play! — home_play scores 0.263 through it vs 1.000 on a clear home — so it belongs to the probe family (reached when home is absent), not the verify_no_* family. Detected by the teal 'News' banner (news_marker: self=1.000, clear home=0.383 — clean separation, no threshold change). Close via the X at (1688,113), CV-verified live 2026-08-01. Re-appears after any client relaunch, which is how it arrived mid-night when adb dropped at 22:26 and the game restarted.

guard_not_news._note: Mid-run twin of probe_news, and the guard whose absence caused the 2026-07-31 livelock: News opened while the loop was in the `running` guard chain, all five guards missed it, and guard_not_inactive.on_absent concluded 'genuinely mid-run' and jumped — 389 cycles over 13h into a popup. probe_news cannot cover this: it is only reachable from the probe side. Same detect, same X.

recover_unknown._note: Progress-watchdog recovery entry (src/fsm.py no_progress_goto). Reached when nothing the config calls progress has happened for no_progress_s — i.e. the screen is something the FSM does not recognise. Detect home first: if the watchdog fired while home was actually up (a stalled run that already ended, say), there is nothing to recover and we rejoin the loop for free. Absent -> recover_unknown_probe, which spends one cheap pass through the known-popup chain before anything drastic.

recover_unknown_probe._note: Cheap half of the recovery: hand to the head of the probe chain, which peels every popup this config has a marker for and ends at home. Costs nothing but poll time and keeps a recognised popup from triggering a restart. If it works, the next watchdog window starts clean; if it does not, the watchdog fires again and lands on recover_unknown_restart — the escalation is the second fire, not extra logic here.

recover_unknown_restart._note: Expensive half, and the one that always works. Verified live 2026-08-01: the Events popup has no marker, is not closed by Android BACK, and survived a full probe-chain walk — the loop simply resumed jumping into it. A screen we cannot identify has no close button we can aim at, so cycle the process instead: restart_app -> recover_login re-auths -> home. Costs a life only if one was mid-run, and by definition the watchdog only fires when no run has been progressing for minutes.

relay_stage1_check_shop_after_run._note: Cookie Relay stage 1/2 (CV-verified live 2026-08-03). The game offers 'Tap to activate Cookie Relay Boost!' whenever a relay partner becomes available — MID-RUN, not only on death (live-confirmed 2026-08-04: 11 hits across three runs, result_marker at 0.32-0.47 on those same frames, i.e. the cookie was still running). An earlier version of this note said 'on death', which is why nothing polled the relay outside the hop chain. with Continue (946,433) above Quit (946,636). Tap Continue — NEVER Quit, which ends the run. Detected by the prompt text (relay_prompt_marker: self=1.000, stage-2=0.736, mid-run=0.387, result=0.489). Absent -> the prompt is not up, resume the run at check_shop_after_run. REPLACES the old blind relay_tap(960,540), which at this stage lands in the gap BETWEEN the two pills and did nothing. FRESH-FRAME WAIT (2026-08-04): the absent path ends with a short wait, not a bare goto. src/fsm.py re-grabs a frame only after a state that DID something; a pure-goto state keeps matching the frame the last acting state (the hop's jump/slide) captured. Without this wait both relay stages judged the same stale frame, so the ~2-3s prompt was caught only by luck — which is exactly why boxrun_toggle never fired the relay while coinrun sometimes did. RETRY REMOVED 2026-08-15: this state carried absent_retries=2 + absent_wait_ms=400, which cost ~5s per visit waiting for a marker that has never matched. Measured across 1,414 archived frames and every log in the repo: relay_prompt_marker scored 0 hits, best 0.673 (and that best frame is the Mailbox 'Send a free Life' dialog, not a relay prompt). The commit that introduced the two-stage chain already recorded why — the green Continue pill never passed 0.40 — because this game build's mid-run relay prompt has no Continue/Quit pair at all: it shows the text plus the cookie's card, and tapping the CARD is what fires it, which is stage 2's job. Five such states (4x stage1 + poll1) were spending ~25s of every ~13s relay-check lap on a guaranteed miss, and the prompt window is only 2-3s, so the retries were directly costing relays. The state itself stays: if a build ever restores the two-button dialog, this is where it gets caught — it just no longer waits around for it.

relay_stage2_check_shop_after_run._note: Cookie Relay stage 2/2. After Continue the same text stays up with the relay cookie's card at (980,515) — tapping THAT is what actually fires the relay (relay_prompt2_marker: self=1.000, stage-1=0.367, mid-run=0.256). Reached both from stage 1 and directly (stage 1 absent), because the two-tap sequence can be caught mid-way on a later hop. Absent -> nothing to do -> resume at check_shop_after_run. The whole prompt window is only ~2-3s, which is why every hop polls this chain instead of checking once per cycle. FRESH-FRAME WAIT (2026-08-04): same reason as stage 1 — without an action here the stage-2 check would re-judge stage 1's frame, i.e. the screen as it was BEFORE the Continue tap landed, and never see the card. THRESHOLD 0.62 (2026-08-04). This template is a text crop whose background is live gameplay, so its score swings with whatever is behind it (coin rain, BONUSTIME flash, star trails). Measured two ways on Episode 5: an 83-frame offline scan scored 0.782/0.815/0.834 on the three frames where the prompt was genuinely up versus <=0.464 on the 80 where it was not; then three live runs fired the relay ELEVEN times, at 0.73/0.76/0.77/0.79/0.80x4/0.83/0.87. The global 0.82 sits INSIDE the 'prompt present' cluster and would have caught 2 of those 11 — about four relays in five were lost silently, visible only as a DEBUG score line. 0.62 sits in the gap: 0.11 below the lowest true positive seen, 0.16 above the highest false one. Stage 1's Continue pill keeps the global threshold — it never passed 0.40 on any frame or in any run.

guard_not_partyrun._note: Close Party Run's 'Select a Mode' screen (added 2026-08-06). This screen had NO marker anywhere in the config, so the bot livelocked on it: every state missed, the guard chain and relay polls kept transitioning normally, and the hop taps landed on a menu instead of a run — a log that reads perfectly healthy while nothing progresses. It is reachable by accident because probe_friendinfo's blind tap (1633,107) lands in the Party Run banner strip when Friend's Info is not actually up (see that state's note). partyrun_marker.png is the purple 'Select a Mode' title bar cropped WITH its background colour — scores 1.000 here and <=0.403 on every other captured frame, unlike a text-only crop whose score would swing with the scene. on_match closes via the X at (1820,135) — the grey circle at the top-right of the SCREEN (area 4919, bbox 80x80 on a live Party Run frame). An earlier version tapped (1638,108), measured off the Friend's Info dialog by mistake; on the Party Run frame that point is dark background (BGR 93,53,51), so the guard detected the screen 38 passes in a row and never closed it. Measure the button on the screen you are closing, not a similar-looking one. CLOSE VERIFIED (2026-08-06): this used tap_xy + goto self, which is how those 38 passes stayed silent — a blind tap cannot tell a wrong coordinate from a slow fade, and self-looping on it produces no log line either way. close_popup re-reads the frame after the settle, taps again while the marker is still up, and log.warning()s if it never clears, exactly like guard_not_news does.

guard_not_friendinfo._note: Mid-run twin of probe_friendinfo, and the third instance of the 2026-07-31 News bug (added 2026-08-14). Friend's Info opens while the loop is in the `running` guard chain — a friend's card can surface on its own — and every guard in that chain missed it, so guard_not_inactive.on_absent concluded 'genuinely mid-run' and jumped into the popup. probe_friendinfo cannot cover this: it is only reachable from the probe side, which is why its hit count across four hours of live logs was ZERO while the player kept seeing the dialog. MEASURED on the archived frame unknown_screens/20260814_223452 (1920x1080, the watchdog happened to catch one): friendinfo_marker scores 0.974, partyrun_marker only 0.384 on the same frame, and the X is a grey circle bbox (1598,68,80,78) centred (1638,107) — pixel (1633,107) inside it reads BGR 255,255,255, i.e. the glyph itself. Same close sequence as probe_friendinfo, including the ROI-scoped inner-X fallback for the two-layer 'Friend's Cookie over Friend's Info' case; goto running rather than home because the run is still live behind the dialog.

probe_sdkfail._note: Failed to connect to server / SDK Code:0 — server-handshake failure at the title screen (added 2026-08-15). ROOT CAUSE OF A 10-HOUR DEAD WINDOW: on 2026-08-14 between 08:00 and 17:00 the bot banked ZERO games while firing the blind watchdog 14-17x/hr and calling restart_app 6-9x/hr. 166 of the 313 frames archived that day are this dialog. No marker matched it, so every state missed, the watchdog escalated to restart_app, the client came back up, failed the handshake again, and the loop repeated every ~7 minutes all day. probe_connectionlost does NOT cover it: that one detects 'Connection lost!' and scores only 0.648 here, below threshold — same dialog frame, different text. MEASURED: sdkfail_marker.png is the 'Failed to connect to server. SDK' text line cropped tight (50x770 at 575,405); 1.000 on all 30 sampled positives, max 0.321 across 60 sampled negatives, margin 0.679. Confirm is the green button, HSV blob bbox (744,614,431,147), centre (959,687). Like Connection lost, Confirm does not dismiss to gameplay — it drops to the title screen, so this hands off to restart_app then recover_login, exactly as probe_connectionlost does. Sits at the HEAD of the probe chain because nothing else in the chain can work while the client is offline.

guard_not_sdkfail._note: Mid-run twin of probe_sdkfail (added 2026-08-15) — the FOURTH instance of the 2026-07-31 News pattern, and the one that cost the most: probe_sdkfail alone would not have caught the 10-hour dead window, because the frames were archived from relay_stage2_jump_3, jump_2 and running, i.e. the mid-run guard chain, where probe_* states are unreachable. Same detect and same Confirm as the probe-side state. Unlike the other guards this one canNOT return to running: Confirm drops the client to the title screen, so the run is already lost and the only correct move is restart_app + recover_login, same as probe_sdkfail.

_no_progress_comment: Progress watchdog (engine-side, src/fsm.py). Reaching any of ['home', 'run_result', 'mystery_box', 'check_heart'] resets the timer; 300s without one means the screen is something the FSM does not recognise — the 2026-07-31 News livelock jumped 389 times over 13h without tripping either existing livelock detector, because state kept changing and jump/slide count as actions. First fire tries the probe chain (recover_unknown); a second fire means that failed, so it cycles the app (recover_unknown_restart) — proven necessary live against the Events popup, which has no marker and ignores Android BACK.
_no_progress_s_comment: Raised 300 -> 600 on 2026-08-15 from measurement, not taste. Across 1,610 real inter-progress gaps in this repo's logs: median 64s, p90 302s, p99 439s — so 300 sat exactly at the p90 and **10.8% of healthy gaps (174 of 1,610) tripped it**. Live example 02:33:23: the wall clock fired on a run that was simply long, the Result popup rendered two seconds later, and the recovery walked the probe chain and reached run_result in 3s — correct behaviour recovering from a false alarm it should never have raised. 600 clears the p99 with 1.4x headroom and still sits well under the blind detector's reach (600 polls at ~0.48/s is ~1250s), so a genuinely stuck screen is still caught by whichever detector trips first. The 1771s max gap in that dataset was the SDK-handshake dead window, i.e. a real fault, and both detectors should fire on that.
